correctness.rationale: The graph follows from exactly m active independent facets at each of m^2+1 vertices. The Laplacian equations are obtained directly from all adjacency families. The zero-row/column symmetric and antisymmetric subspaces contribute eigenvalues m and m+2 with multiplicities m(m-3)/2 and (m-1)(m-2)/2. Orthogonal complement yields scalar 3x3 and m-1 standard 3x3 blocks, accounting for all dimensions. Their determinants match the stated quadratic/cubic, yielding the exact spanning-tree count by the matrix-tree theorem. Cubic monotonicity on (0,2), the quadratic lower-root bound, and signs at 1 and 1+1/m establish the spectral gap. Exact finite integer calculations are supplementary.

originality.rationale: The source papers establish the partial-permutohedron vertices, face lattice, explicit P(m,2) inequalities and Ehrhart polynomial, not the full Laplacian polynomial or spanning-tree product. The theorem also is not entailed by standard clique insertion: that operation inserts a clique at every source vertex, whereas the present one-skeleton has a unique surviving untruncated apex. Search across synonyms, relevant published mathematical findings, and the primary literature found no stronger/equivalent result. Existing results about inballs and Euclidean diameters of partial permutohedra, and spanning trees of unrelated coherent-path graphs, do not imply this graph-spectral calculation. Alternate terminology remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent spectrum for a partially truncated complete graph under different terminology could have escaped the searches.
The complete article on fully clique-inserted graphs was not fully available via the accessed renderer; the operation was distinguished using its independently documented definition and graph order.
Literature comparisons are not independent verification and do not examine unpublished work.

value.rationale: The second-parameter-two partial permutohedra form the first non-simplex case in a well-motivated family already studied for faces, Ehrhart polynomials and volume. Their m^2+1-vertex m-regular graphs have graph reliability and spectral connectivity invariants not supplied by those geometric statistics. The all-m theorem factors a growing characteristic polynomial into two small-degree factors and two integer eigenvalue families and gives a closed tree count and a nontrivial bounded spectral-gap regime; these are natural exact structural invariants, not a narrow arbitrary numerical table.
